title: The Mutators Reloaded: Fuzzing Compilers with Large Language Model Generated Mutation Operators
problem: Creating high-quality mutation operators for compiler fuzzing requires deep compiler expertise, extensive manual effort, and knowledge of compiler internals. Existing approaches lack generalizability and scalability for generating domain-specific fuzzing strategies.
motivation: Effective mutation operators are essential for fuzzing compilers like GCC and Clang to discover critical bugs in foundational infrastructure used across the computing industry.
method: MetaMut integrates compiler-domain knowledge into LLM prompts and processes to automatically generate semantic-aware mutation operators. The framework uses LLMs to synthesize mutators that understand compiler semantics, then deploys these mutators in a fuzzer to explore the compiler's behavior space and uncover bugs.
key_novelty: Automated LLM-driven generation of domain-specific mutation operators that eliminate the need for expert manual implementation while maintaining semantic correctness.
contributions: MetaMut framework for automated compiler mutation operator generation using LLMs
118 semantic-aware mutators created at approximately $0.50 per mutator with moderate human effort
Discovery of 131 bugs in GCC and Clang compilers, with 129 confirmed or fixed
Demonstration that AI can automate complex software engineering tasks traditionally requiring expert domain knowledge

metrics.other: 131 bugs discovered; 129 confirmed/fixed; 118 mutators at $0.50 each

limitations: Scope limited to compiler fuzzing; generalizability to other software testing domains and scaling properties not discussed.
primary_theme: LLM-driven automated mutation operator synthesis for compiler fuzzing
